subject: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)

Team —

Quick ask: BrightDesk (Samir Khan) is running a 6-week pilot starting May 3. They asked for a guaranteed headroom slice (2x their booked capacity) so their latency-sensitive flows remain stable during expected traffic bursts. Sales is ready to sign a short amendment (we'd take cost pass-through), but we need a technical & ops signoff for an autoscale exception / temporary reservation.

Key constraints and asks:
- Duration requested: 2027-05-03 -> 2027-06-14 (6 weeks)
- Region: us-west1 (preferred)
- Headroom size: +2x of baseline pilot slice (estimate: additional 8 vGPU equivalents)
- Hard requirement: sub-150ms 95th token latency for the pilot service
- Contracting: BrightDesk will accept a usage surcharge if we attach cost tracking

What I need from you by COB Mon:
1) Kimberly: operational feasibility + suggested mitigation (ephemeral slice vs carveout) and estimate of collateral impact on other pilots.
2) Jonas: can infra support a temporary autoscale exception and what runbook changes are needed for preemption?
3) Laura/Grace/Marcus: product/business acceptability (SLA/monitoring/rollback criteria).

Attaching the BrightDesk ask doc for context. Happy to sync quick in person if helpful.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Revenue & Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightDesk_Pilot_Ask.pdf (pdf, 1 page)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)

Thanks Aditya —

From a product perspective we can accept a temporary carveout but with conservative guardrails:
- Scope the carveout to the pilot's endpoint only (avoid broad model-level reservations).
- Require an automated rollback trigger: if mean token latency increases >10% for our baseline customers for >15 minutes, slice is cut back immediately.
- BrightDesk must provide the exact traffic pattern estimate (p50/p95 concurrency) by EOD Tue so we can size properly.

If operations can give a 4-week window instead of 6, product will greenlight faster. We can ramp the pilot traffic over 48 hours to reduce cold-start risk.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly: operational recommendation + impact spreadsheet (matching pilot_rollout_timeline).
- Jonas: quick list of runbook additions and on-call escalation path.

Attaching a timeline I sketched.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Group PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot_rollout_timeline.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)

Folks —

Operational note and proposal after looking at current pool utilization and queued pilots:

1) Feasibility: We can provision an ephemeral slice for BrightDesk in us-west1 for the requested window, but 6 weeks as a full reserved carveout will materially increase risk to 3 other in-flight pilots (shared staging and two small enterprise pilots).

2) Recommendation (preferred):
- Approve a 4-week ephemeral slice (2027-05-03 to 2027-05-31) with the option for a 2-week extension pending a capacity review and approval from Product + Revenue.
- Implement a soft throttling policy: cap burst to 3x baseline for short windows (5m) and require manual approval for sustained >3x usage.
- Cost model: BrightDesk is billed for actual usage + a 20% service premium to cover priority scheduling. We can log usage to the BrightDesk deal in HubSpot for invoicing.

3) Mitigations:
- We'll isolate the slice to the pilot route only and add KV/prefix caching rules to reduce hot-start costs.
- If a higher-priority pilot needs capacity, ops will flag a rollback; product rollback criteria (Laura) must be actionable.

Questions for leadership:
- Is revenue ok with the 20% premium and a potential shorter window?
- Aditya: will you accept the 4+2 approval pattern so team can proceed?

I'll draft the allocation ticket and attach runbook changes once we confirm.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 12:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)

Thanks — technical confirm from infra side. Summary: we can support an ephemeral slice with an autoscale-exception policy. Implementation notes:

- Provisioning: create ephemeral slice in us-west1 tagged brightdesk-pilot-DEAL-8347. It will use a preemptible-backed pool with QoS shaping to meet 95th token latency target under the capped burst profiles Kimberly suggested.
- Runbook changes: add immediate rollback action (playbook step) if cluster-level token latency drift >10% for baseline customers for >10 minutes. I've drafted the runbook changes here: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/OPS/ephemeral-slice-runbook (see section "pilot headroom flow").
- Monitoring: New dashboard (redwood.ops/brightdesk-DEAL-8347) with token-latency, per-route QPS, and throttle events; alerts to infra-oncall + ops-leads.
- Gate: we will only approve the initial 4 weeks. Any extension requires explicit product signoff and a pre-approval checklist that Kimberly will run.

I'll spin up a staging slice for internal validation on Tue 2027-04-06. Ops will be on-call the first 72 hours of production.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
Attachments: temporary-slice-runbook.md (md, 5kb)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightdesk.com>, BrightDesk Procurement <procurement@brightdesk.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom for BrightDesk pilot (autoscale exception)

Appreciate the quick turn. Kim/Jonas — proceed with the 4-week ephemeral slice + optional 2-week extension with the conditions you outlined. Laura/Grace — please confirm product will run the rollback criteria and accept the monitoring terms. Sales: I'll send the amendment to Samir after we finalize the exact vGPU count (Kim will provide numbers).

Samir — thanks for your flexibility on the window. Procurement—expect an amendment for signature (usage + 20% premium).

I'll mark this as approved for ops to begin ticketing and staging validation.

—Aditya
